target_customer: Mid-market e-commerce brands doing roughly 3 to 100 million dollars in annual sales
problem: E-commerce brands need credit and spend tools sized to inventory and ad spend, but traditional bank cards and corporate card startups offer limits and underwriting that do not fit their cash cycles.
business_model: Corporate charge card with interchange and credit revenue, financed by debt facilities, plus software and finance tools bundle
product_category: E-commerce corporate card and financial platform

founders.name: Yacine Sibous
founders.background_notes: Fintech Global quotes him saying he and his co-founder were e-commerce entrepreneurs who built the tools they wished they had.

founders.name: Milan Ray
education: University of Michigan, engineering (from YC bio line 'ex-42 & UMich Engineering', not separately confirmed)
founders.background_notes: YC bio: ex-42 and UMich Engineering, working on e-commerce and fintech projects.

exit.reason: Co-founder said a planned acquisition worth nearly 90 million dollars fell through and the company filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on about 7 May 2026; he also cited leadership turnover, a tougher market and slowing growth.

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing through sponsor banks, underwriting for e-commerce cash flows and software integrations; standard fintech engineering with credit risk modeling.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on partner banks (Patriot Bank, Piermont Bank) and debt facilities; larger corporate card issuers could target the same segment.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in 2023 framed Parker as competing with Brex and Ramp; no copying documented. A planned acquisition near 90 million dollars collapsed in 2026.

market_need_then: The YC listing from the 2019 batch only says 'digital bank'; the e-commerce credit focus emerged around 2023 and no 2019 demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Used getparker.com, not parker.com, which belongs to other companies.
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage was mostly funding and shutdown news; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared with Parker pens, Parker Hannifin and others; brand awareness came from funding press, not from a distinctive identity.

pivots.to: Charge card and finance platform for e-commerce brands
pivots.why: Company emerged from stealth in 2023 with the e-commerce card; the YC description stayed 'digital bank'

outcome_analysis: Parker went from a Winter 2019 digital bank idea to an e-commerce credit card that raised a 31.1 million dollar Series A and large debt facilities in 2023, a 20 million dollar Series B in 2024, and a reported 125 million dollars in 2025. In May 2026 it filed for Chapter 7 after a roughly 90 million dollar acquisition collapsed. The founder cited leadership turnover, a tougher market and slowing growth, so the factor assignments here are interpretive rather than stated, and the exact credit economics are not public.
notes: getparker.com returned HTTP 404. The seed amount is the previously unannounced 5.9M seed and pre-seed combined, per the March 2023 announcement. Debt conflict: FinTech Futures says 120M debt (Triple Point venture debt, Jefferies warehouse), Fintech Global says 70M plus an uncommitted 50M option; the 157M headline appears to include the option. Series B (2024-11, 20M, Valar lead) is confirmed by the company blog, a law firm release and American Bazaar; the company blog states total 178M. The 2025-09 125M figure rests on one outlet (PYMNTS) and another source calls it a lending arrangement, so stage is other. Total funding figures conflict across sources (127.5M CB Insights, 171M ZoomInfo, 178M company, over 200M PYMNTS). The YC page lists location as New York while a search summary said San Francisco. Competitors left empty: no source dated near January 2019 naming rivals was found; 2023 coverage names Brex and Ramp, too late for as_of. An interviewpal claim of about 150 laid off staff is from a single job tracking site and not used.
